name: manual_92d985
claim: A subprocess worker pool that only calls proc.kill() on timeout leaves grandchild processes running: kill() signals the direct python -c child only, not any process it spawns itself. Fix: launch each worker with start_new_session=True (own process group), then on timeout send os.killpg(pid, SIGTERM) first (let it clean up), escalate to os.killpg(pid, SIGKILL) if it doesn't exit within a few seconds. Separately, redirect worker stdout/stderr to temp files instead of subprocess.PIPE -- a chatty worker writing more than the OS pipe buffer (~64KB) deadlocks against a poll loop that only drains pipes after the worker exits; files never fill up under the writer, and CLAYGO cleanup (os.remove after reading) keeps them from accumulating.

decisions.notes: CodeRabbit PR #280 review (orama-system) on hermes_delegate.py's subprocess worker redesign: caught both the grandchild-survives-timeout bug and the pipe-deadlock risk. Verified the grandchild fix with a real regression test (test_subprocess_worker_timeout_kills_grandchild) that spawns an actual grandchild process and confirms it's dead after the parent's timeout, not just trusting the code review.
